SpecialFlags.description:
This field is a bitmask and is for controlling server side quest functions. Blizzard keeps these data server-side and they are not sent to the client, so we have to populate the field manually.

excerpt from [`enum QuestSpecialFlags`](https://github.com/TrinityCore/TrinityCore/tree/3.3.5/src/server/game/Quests/QuestDef.h):
SpecialFlags.hint: This field is a bitmask and is for controlling server side quest functions.

values.name: QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAGS_EXPLORATION_OR_EVENT
values.comment: if required area explore, spell SPELL_EFFECT_QUEST_COMPLETE casting, an entry in areatrigger_involvedrelation or _script command SCRIPT_COMMAND_QUEST_EXPLORED use

values.name: QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAGS_AUTO_ACCEPT
values.comment: if the quest is to be auto-accepted. As of patch 3.3.5a only quests in the starter area need this flag.

values.name: QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAGS_DF_QUEST
values.comment: if the quest is used by Dungeon Finder.

values.name: QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAGS_MONTHLY
values.comment: if the quest is reset at the begining of the month

values.name: QUEST_SPECIAL_FLAGS_CAST
values.comment: if the quest requires RequiredOrNpcGo killcredit but NOT kill (a spell cast). This action usually involves "killing" an invisible "bunny" NPC.

VerifiedBuild.description:
This field is used by the TrinityDB Team to determine whether a template has been verified from WDB files.

If value is 0 then it has not been parsed yet.

skill_discovery_template.title: skill_discovery_template
skill_discovery_template.description: This table controls the so called "discovery" system of learning spells. This system is used by the alchemy and inscription profession and controls the chance for a player to "discover" another recipe while creating items with known recipes.

spellId.description: The recipe [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) that has a chance to be automatically discovered.
spellId.hint: The recipe Spell ID that has a chance to be automatically discovered.

reqSpell.description:
* **reqSpell** = 0: Any recipe spell can trigger the discovery
* **reqSpell** > 0: Must use a specific recipe to trigger the discovery (e.g.: [Cauldron of Major Arcane Protection](aowow.trinitycore.info/?spell=41458) will only be discovered while using [Major Arcane Protection Potion](https://aowow.trinitycore.info/?spell=28575)).
reqSpell.hint: reqSpell = 0: Any recipe spell can trigger the discovery reqSpell > 0: Must use a specific recipe to trigger the discovery (e.g.: Cauldron of Major Arcane Protection will only be discovered while using Major Arcane Protection Potion).

reqSkillValue.description: The minimum points requirement in profession skill to discover **spellId**.
reqSkillValue.hint: The minimum points requirement in profession skill to discover spellId.

chance.description: The chance, in percent, that a recipe has of being automatically "discovered", whether by any recipe use or by the specific recipe use defined in **reqSpell**.
chance.hint: The chance, in percent, that a recipe has of being automatically "discovered", whether by any recipe use or by the specific recipe use defined in reqSpell.

skill_extra_item_template.title: skill_extra_item_template
skill_extra_item_template.description: This table holds information about when using certain profession spells will create more than one copy of the item. (Alchemy specializations)

spellId.description: The [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) that creates the item.
spellId.hint: The Spell ID that creates the item.

requiredSpecialization.description: The character must have the [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the extra item proc.
requiredSpecialization.hint: The character must have the Spell ID specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the extra item proc.

additionalCreateChance.description: The chance that the player will create an additional item.
additionalCreateChance.hint: The chance that the player will create an additional item.

additionalMaxNum.description:
The number of extra copies that can be created.
**additionalCreateChance** is rolled for each attempt, until failure or reaching **additionalMaxNum**.
additionalMaxNum.hint: The number of extra copies that can be created.

skill_fishing_base_level.title: skill_fishing_base_level
skill_fishing_base_level.description: This table controls the minimum skill level required in SKILL_FISHING (356), to fish in a certain area with 100% success. > Note: This does not affect fishing from fishing nodes.

entry.description: references [AreaTable ID](/files/DBC/335/areatable#id)

skill.description:
The minimum skill points in fishing required to fish in the area without receiving trash.

If the player is less skilled, the chance to fish successfully is as follows:
* `chance = MAX(1; (playerSkill / areaSkill)^2 * 100)`
skill.hint: The minimum skill points in fishing required to fish in the area without receiving trash.

skill_perfect_item_template.title: skill_perfect_item_template
skill_perfect_item_template.description: This table holds information about when using certain profession spells will create a different version of the item. (Jewelcrafting - Gem Perfection)

spellId.hint: Spell ID that creates the item.

requiredSpecialization.description: The character must have the [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the effect.
requiredSpecialization.hint: The character must have the Spell ID specified here learned to have a chance at triggering the effect.

perfectCreateChance.description: The chance that the player will create an alternative item.
perfectCreateChance.hint: The chance that the player will create an alternative item.

perfectItemType.description: The [item entry](../world/item_template#entry) replacing the original crafted item.
perfectItemType.hint: The item entry replacing the original crafted item.

skinning_loot_template.title: skinning_loot_template
skinning_loot_template.description: Contains items generated when using a spell with SPELL_EFFECT_SKINNING(95) on a creature. [Please refer to the generic description of the loot system for more information.](/database/335/world/loot_template)

smart_scripts.title: smart_scripts
smart_scripts.description: > Manual editing smart_scripts table can be tedious and difficult, for easier writing scripts you can use additional TrinityCore tools like [WoW Database Editor](https://github.com/TrinityCore/WoWDatabaseEditor/).

entryorguid.description:
* **source_type** = 9: invoking **entryorguid** * 100 (+i, if multiple timed action lists are set)
* **entryorguid** > 0: entry of the creature / game object / etc.
* **entryorguid** < 0: guid of the creature / game object / etc.
entryorguid.hint: source_type = 9: invoking entryorguid 100 (+i, if multiple timed action lists are set) entryorguid > 0: entry of the creature / game object / etc.

id.description: Incremental id bound to each **entryorguid** + **source_type** (0, 1, 2, ...).
id.hint: Incremental id bound to each entryorguid + source_type (0, 1, 2, ...).

link.description:
Simple event linking;
Example: if **id** = 0 and **link** = 1; **id** 1 will only be able to occur if **id** = 0 was triggered.
link.hint: Simple event linking; Example: if id = 0 and link = 1; id 1 will only be able to occur if id = 0 was triggered.

Difficulties.description:
Comma-separated list of difficulties where only the event can occur. `''` means everywhere.
> **Examples**:
> * '' → Everywhere
> * '0' → Open world
> * '1,2' → Dungeon normal/heroic
> * '0,3' → Open world and Raid 10 Player
> * '3,4,5,6' → Raid 10/25 normal/heroic

event_phase_mask.description:
When dealing with phases, phase IDs have to be used. There are 13 (12+1) different phases: 1, 2, ... 12 and the default 0.

Example: The script is in phase 0 by default - If we want it to go to phase 1, we got two choices:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 1 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 1

If the script is in phase 0 and want to skip to phase 2:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 2 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 2

If the script is in phase 1 and want to skip to phase 2:
 SMART_ACTION_INC_PHASE by 1 or SMART_ACTION_SET_PHASE 2
event_phase_mask.hint: When dealing with phases, phase IDs have to be used.

event_chance.description: This is the probability of the event to occur as a percentage from 0-100. So, if you want the event to occur roughly half of the time, then set this to 50.

spawn_group.title: spawn_group
spawn_group.description: This table contains Spawn Group members.

spawnId.description: This is the guid of the creature/gameobject included in the group.
spawnId.hint: This is the guid of the creature/gameobject included in the group.

spawn_group_template.title: spawn_group_template
spawn_group_template.description: This table contains Spawn Group names and flags. Spawn Groups are collections of creatures / gameobjects, linked to scripted events or boss fights.

groupId.description:
This is the ID for the group. It must be a unique number.
> Groups 0 – 4 are reserved for system tasks.
groupId.hint: This is the ID for the group.

groupName.description:
This is a descriptive name for the group, like: `[zone] - [related event] - [group content]`
e.g.: `Halls of Lightning - General Bjarngrim - Stormforged Lieutenants`
groupName.hint: This is a descriptive name for the group, like: [zone] - [related event] - [group content] e.g.: Halls of Lightning - General Bjarngrim - Stormforged Lieutenants

SpawnTrackingId.description: SpawnTracking ID for the spawn. It must match a SpawnTracking already existing in the [spawn_tracking_template](/en/database/master/world/spawn_tracking_template) table.

SpawnId.description:
Spawn ID/GUID of the creature/game object that should be included in the group. The GUID must exist in the [creature](/en/database/master/world/creature) or [gameobject](/en/database/master/world/gameobject) tables respectively.

> Spawn must use the same Map, Phase, PhaseGroup and PhaseUseFlags as the SpawnTracking template.
SpawnId.hint: Spawn ID/GUID of the creature/game object that should be included in the group.

QuestObjectiveIds.description:
Valid [quest_objectives.Ids](/en/database/master/world/quest_objectives#id).
Some SpawnTrackings are reused for several quest objectives so spawn's state changes will be checked for all of them (priority will be the completed objectives and then the active ones).

SpawnTrackingId.description: SpawnTracking ID linked to the quest objective. It must match a SpawnTracking already existing in the [spawn_tracking_template](/en/database/master/world/spawn_tracking_template) table.
SpawnTrackingId.hint: SpawnTracking ID linked to the quest objective.

QuestObjectiveId.description:
An existing [quest_objectives.Id](/en/database/master/world/quest_objectives#id).
Some SpawnTrackings are reused for several quest objectives.

VerifiedBuild.description:
This field is used by the TrinityDB Team to determine whether a template has been verified from WDB files.

If value is 0 then it has not been parsed yet.

If value is above 0 then it has been parsed with WDB files from that specific client build.

If value is -1 then it is just a place holder until proper data are found on WDBs.

If value is -Client Build then it was parsed with WDB files from that specific client build and manually edited later for some special necessity.
VerifiedBuild.hint: This field is used by the TrinityDB Team to determine whether a template has been verified from WDB files.

spell_area.title: spell_area
spell_area.description: This table is used to apply a specific spell aura to the player within an area in the game. When any player enters this area or somehow interacts with a quest, this aura will be handled accordingly.

spell.description: The [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) to be casted on the player.
spell.hint: The Spell ID to be casted on the player.

area.description: The [AreaTable ID](/files/DBC/335/areatable#id) where **spell** should be applied.
area.hint: The AreaTable ID where spell should be applied.

quest_start.description: The [Quest ID](../world/quest_template#id) which the player must have in the state defined by **quest_start_status** for the spell to apply.
quest_start.hint: The Quest ID which the player must have in the state defined by quest_start_status for the spell to apply.

quest_end.description:
The [Quest ID](../world/quest_template#id) which the player must not have in the state defined by **quest_end_status** for the spell to apply.
Setting both quest_start and quest_end to the same value is useless.
quest_end.hint: The Quest ID which the player must not have in the state defined by quest_end_status for the spell to apply.

aura_spell.description:
If set, this value (plus or minus aura [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id)) imposes additional condition.
* **aura_spell** < 0: If the player has aura **-aura_spell** then **spell** will not be activated.
* **aura_spell** = 0: This column is ignored.
* **aura_spell** > 0: If the player has no aura **aura_spell** then **spell** will not be activated.
aura_spell.hint: If set, this value (plus or minus aura Spell ID) imposes additional condition.

racemask.description: Race mask of [ChrRace IDs](/files/DBC/335/chrraces#id) **spell** applies to. (0: any race)
racemask.hint: Race mask of ChrRace IDs spell applies to.

gender.description:
The player gender this entry applies to.

[`enum Gender`](https://github.com/TrinityCore/TrinityCore/blob/3.3.5/src/server/shared/SharedDefines.h#L75-L80)
gender.hint: The player gender this entry applies to.

values.name: SPELL_AREA_FLAG_AUTOCAST

spell_trigger.description: The [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id), which when cast, will trigger the spell listed in **spell_effect**.

spell_effect.hint: The Spell ID that you want to be triggered.

type.description:
Describes how both spells are linked * 0: SPELL_LINK_CAST | -- | -- | -- | | | **spell_trigger > 0** | **spell_trigger < 0** | | **spell_effect > 0** | When spell_trigger is cast
spell_effect is also cast (as triggered cast) on the same targets, or caster. | When the aura of spell_trigger is removed
spell_effect is also cast (as triggered cast) on the same targets, or caster. | | **spell_effect < 0** | When spell_trigger is cast
auras of spell_effect are removed. | When the aura of spell_trigger is removed
auras of spell_effect are removed. | * 1: SPELL_LINK_HIT | -- | -- | -- | | | **spell_trigger > 0** | **spell_trigger < 0** | | **spell_effect > 0** | When spell_trigger hits it's target
spell_effect is cast (as triggered cast) on the same target. | *- invalid -* | | **spell_effect < 0** | When spell_trigger hits it's target
auras of spell_effect are removed. | *- invalid -* | * 2: SPELL_LINK_AURA | -- | -- | -- | -- | | | **spell_trigger > 0** | **spell_trigger < 0** | | **spell_effect > 0** | While aura of spell_trigger is applied
aura of spell_effect is also applied on the same target. | *- invalid -* | | **spell_effect < 0** | While aura of spell_trigger is applied
target is immune to spell_effect. | *- invalid -* |
type.hint: Describes how both spells are linked 0: SPELL_LINK_CAST 1: SPELL_LINK_HIT 2: SPELL_LINK_AURA

comment.hint: Optional comment to explain the link.

date_value.description:
Start date in BlizzTime. Use https://github.com/The-Cataclysm-Preservation-Project/Packet-BlizzTime-tool to get the correct value.

> From wowdev.wiki:
> Packed blizzdate (integers with bits (LSB->MSB) 6: minutes, 5: hours, 3: day of week, 6: day of month, 4: month, 5: year, 2: time zone, 1: unused)
> Epochdate=01.01.2000-00:00

**Example**
Startdate for Darkmoon Faire - Mulgore (first occurence):
```
blizzdate = 126957568;                    // 0b0000 0111 1001 0001 0011 1000 0000 0000

minutes    =  blizzdate        & 0x3F;    // 00 0000 -> 0
hours      = (blizzdate >>  6) & 0x1F;    //  0 0000 -> 0
dayOfWeek  = (blizzdate >> 11) & 0x07;    //     111 -> 7
dayOfMonth = (blizzdate >> 14) & 0x3F;    // 00 0100 -> 4
month      = (blizzdate >> 20) & 0x0F;    //    1001 -> 9
year       = (blizzdate >> 24) & 0x1F;    //  0 0111 -> 7
timeZone   = (blizzdate >> 29) & 0x03;    //      00 -> 0
padding    = (blizzdate >> 31) & 0x01;    //       0

decoded: 0007-09-04T00:00:00+00:00
apply epoch date offset
realdate: 2007-10-05T00:00:00
```

RandomProperty.description:
The number in this field points to [item_enchantment_template.entry](../world/item_enchantment_template#entry) and ties in an item's chance at having a random property attached to it when it is generated.
The items enchantments are then ultimately derived from [ItemRandomProperties](/files/DBC/335/itemrandomproperties)

This field and the **RandomSuffix** field CANNOT both have non-zero values.
RandomProperty.hint: The number in this field points to item_enchantment_template.entry and ties in an item's chance at having a random property attached to it when it is generated.

RandomSuffix.description:
The number in this field points to [item_enchantment_template.entry](../world/item_enchantment_template#entry) and ties in an item's chance at having a random suffix attached to it when it is generated.
The items enchantments are then ultimately derived from [ItemRandomSuffix](/files/DBC/335/itemrandomsuffix)

This field and the **RandomProperty** field CANNOT both have non-zero values.
RandomSuffix.hint: The number in this field points to item_enchantment_template.entry and ties in an item's chance at having a random suffix attached to it when it is generated.

references [ItemPetFood ID](/files/DBC/335/itempetfood#id)

VerifiedBuild.description:
This field is used by the TrinityDB Team to determine whether a template has been verified from WDB files.

If value is 0 then it has not been parsed yet.

If value is above 0 then it has been parsed with WDB files from that specific [client build](/en/database/335/auth/realmlist#gamebuild).

If value is -1 then it is just a place holder until proper data are found on WDBs.

If value is -[Client Build](/en/database/335/auth/realmlist#gamebuild) then it was parsed with WDB files from that specific client build and manually edited later for some special necessity.
VerifiedBuild.hint: This field is used by the TrinityDB Team to determine whether a template has been verified from WDB files.

playercreateinfo_skills.description: This table holds information on what skills newly created characters should start out with. A character in this table is defined by his/her race and class combination.

classMask.description: Class id mask from [ChrClass ID](/files/DBC/335/chrclasses#id). `0` is all classes.
classMask.hint: Class id mask from ChrClass ID.

skill.hint: A SkillLine ID to start with.

rank.description: If the skill has ranks set in [SkillTiers](/files/DBC/335/skilltiers) the desired starting rank (and thus starting skill value) can be specified here as [SkillTiers Value](/files/DBC/335/skilltiers#value) index.

script_waypoint.description: This table holds creature waypoints for use by the scripting system.

entry.description: A [creature_template.entry](../world/creature_template#entry). This creature must have a [ScriptName](../world/creature_template#scriptname) assigned.

pointid.description: Unique ID for each waypoint. Starts at 1 and increases with each waypoint.

location_x.description: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.
location_x.hint: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.

location_y.description: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.
location_y.hint: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.

location_z.description: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.
location_z.hint: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.

waittime.description: Time in milliseconds to wait at waypoint.
waittime.hint: Time in milliseconds to wait at waypoint.

point_comment.description: This field is for any comment you want to make. It is arbitrary text.
point_comment.hint: This field is for any comment you want to make.

scripts.title: *_scripts
scripts.description: This table format is used for 2 different tables to control possible scripts activated by different actions: * **[event_scripts](../world/event_scripts)**: Holds scripts activated whenever an event is activated, be it by an object or as the spell effect SPELL_EFFECT_SEND_EVENT (61). * **[waypoint_scripts](../world/waypoint_scripts)**: Holds scripts used in the waypoint_data table. > Note: An entry in this table may have more than one row as a script may do more than just one action. Also each action the script may make can have a separate delay attached to it. In that case, the core will activate the appropriate action after the correct delay.

id.description:
* `spell_scripts`: [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id)
* `waypoint_scripts`: [waypoint_data.action](../world/waypoint_data#action)
* `event_scripts`: an event ID. There doesn't exist currently a full list of events. In any case, the event IDs are taken directly from gameobject WDB data or spell effect data. If both a gameobject and a spell activate the same event, the IDs will match.
id.hint: spell_scripts: Spell ID waypoint_scripts: waypoint_data.action event_scripts: an event ID.

delay.description: Delay in seconds before this current step of the script activates. 0 = instant.
delay.hint: Delay in seconds before this current step of the script activates.

command.description:
The type of action performed by the script after **delay** has passed. The value of this field affects what other fields also need to be set.
The following commands can be used:
command.hint: The type of action performed by the script after delay has passed.

values.name: FIELD_SET
values.comment: Change the value at an index for the player.

values.name: FLAG_SET
values.comment: Turns on bits on a flag field at an index for the player.

values.name: FLAG_REMOVE
values.comment: Turns off bits on a flag field at an index for the player.

values.name: TELEPORT_TO
values.comment: Teleports the player to a location.

values.name: QUEST_EXPLORED
values.comment: Satisfies the explore requirement for a quest.

values.name: KILL_CREDIT
values.comment: Gives kill credit to the player.

values.name: REMOVE_AURA
values.comment: Removes an aura due to a spell.

values.name: CREATE_ITEM
values.comment: Creates specified amount of items for the player.

values.name: LOAD_PATH
values.comment: Load path to unit, then unit starts waypoint movement.

values.name: CALLSCRIPT_TO_UNIT
values.comment: Calls script from one of _scripts table with given unit as source.

values.name: KILL
values.comment: Changes state of the creature to dead and optionally removes its corpse.

values.name: ORIENTATION
values.comment: Changes unit's orientation (Used in Waypoint Scripts)

values.name: CLOSE_GOSSIP
values.comment: Closes gossip window. This command is only used for Gossip Scripts.

guid.description:
Acts as primary key for waypoint_scripts. It is set automatically using the GM command `.wp event add`.
> Note: only present in [waypoint_scripts](../world/waypoint_scripts)
guid.hint: Acts as primary key for waypoint_scripts.

Comment.description: This field is for any comment you want to make. It is arbitrary text.
Comment.hint: This field is for any comment you want to make.

spell_bonus_data.title: spell_bonus_data
spell_bonus_data.description: Table used for storing custom damage/healing bonus coefficients.

entry.description:
references [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id)
Only the first rank of the spell needs data if spell exists in [spell_ranks](../world/spell_ranks) and coefficients are the same for each rank.
entry.hint: references Spell ID Only the first rank of the spell needs data if spell exists in spell_ranks and coefficients are the same for each rank.

direct_bonus.description: Spell Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.
direct_bonus.hint: Spell Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.

dot_bonus.description: Spell Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.
dot_bonus.hint: Spell Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.

ap_bonus.description: Attack Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.
ap_bonus.hint: Attack Power coefficient for the direct damage/healing component of the spell.

ap_dot_bonus.description:
Attack Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.

#### for all fields:
* `0 <= bonus <= 1`: 0%  – 100% scaling
* `-1`: Uses generic scaling depending on cast time and aura duration.
ap_dot_bonus.hint: Attack Power coefficient for the over time component of the spell.

comments.description:
commonly: Spell User – Spell Name
e.g.: `Item - Onyxia 10 Caster Trinket - Searing Flames`
comments.hint: commonly: Spell User – Spell Name e.g.: Item - Onyxia 10 Caster Trinket - Searing Flames

spell_dbc.title: spell_dbc
spell_dbc.description: Structurally similar to the [Spell.dbc](/files/DBC/335/spell) file, this table holds supplemental data on spells referenced by, but missing from the [Spell.dbc](/files/DBC/335/spell) file.

spell_ranks.title: spell_ranks
spell_ranks.description: Table used by the core to group different ranks of spells (the gray text seen on ranked spells) into one "spell stem". This partly involves checks for aura stacking (e.g. different levels of the same spell). One spell can not be linked to multiple rank chains (they are "unique").

first_spell_id.description: [Spell ID](/files/DBC/335/spell#id) which is first rank of spell rank chain. It identifies the whole chain.
first_spell_id.hint: Spell ID which is first rank of spell rank chain.

rank.description:
An integer which ranks the spell within the chain of spell ranks for the given **spell_id**. It can differ from the rank text in game (for example, some ranks in client start with level 0, while the server always starts from level 1 onward).

Several conditions have to be fulfilled:
* At least two ranks are required.
* The ranking must be continuous (e.g. one spell being level 3 and one being level 5 while level 4 is missing altogether)
* There can be no duplicates in ranks.
rank.hint: An integer which ranks the spell within the chain of spell ranks for the given spell_id.

spelldifficulty_dbc.title: spelldifficulty_dbc
spelldifficulty_dbc.description: Structurally identical to the [SpellDifficulty.dbc](/files/DBC/335/spelldifficulty) file, this table holds supplemental data. The id is called in the cpp script and depending on what version of the dungeon/raid the characters are in, the proper SpellID will be casted by the creature.

id.description: *- no description -*

waypoint_data.title: waypoint_data
waypoint_data.description: This table contains all the path data for creatures that use waypoints.

id.description:
Unique ID for each path.

The TDB standard way of assigning an ID is to multiply [creature guid](../world/creature#guid) by 10.

So for a creature with a GUID of 1234 the path ID would be 12340. Any waypoints submitted to TDB should follow this standard.

However, this is only a suggestion when creating your own waypoints. This ID can be anything you want as long as [path_id](../world/creature_addon#path_id) is set to the **id** you pick here for the creature you are creating a waypoint for.

point.description: Unique point ID for each point in a path. Starts at 1 and increases with each path node.
point.hint: Unique point ID for each point in a path.

position_x.description: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.
position_x.hint: The X coordinate of the destination waypoint.

position_y.description: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.
position_y.hint: The Y coordinate of the destination waypoint.

position_z.description: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.
position_z.hint: The Z coordinate of the destination waypoint.

orientation.description: The orientation of the creature. (North = 0.0; South = π (3.14159))

delay.description: Time to wait (in ms) before moving to the next point.
delay.hint: Time to wait (in ms) before moving to the next point.

action.description: [Script ID](../world/waypoint_scripts#id) of the action to be performed.
action.hint: Script ID of the action to be performed.

wpguid.description:
This field is used by the core and is _NOT_ to be set by hand.

This field holds the GUID of the waypoint visual when you enable the visual mode for waypoints.
wpguid.hint: This field is used by the core and is _NOT_ to be set by hand.

waypoint_scripts.description: Holds scripts used in the [waypoint_data](../world/waypoint_data) table. [Please refer to the generic description of the script system for more information.](/database/335/world/scripts)
